interpretation: Invarune-authored explanations of the existing engineering controls. Source relationships are contextual provenance or thematic alignment, not official clause-level compliance mappings. No model, scan or runtime validation occurs when exploring this catalog.

controls.what_it_is: Maintain a reconciled inventory of the components that can read data, make decisions or execute actions.
controls.why_it_matters: An unregistered tool or endpoint can inherit access without a responsible owner or security review.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Include the deployed agent harness, model revision, MCP transport and exposed tools; a repository dependency list alone is not the running inventory.

controls.what_it_is: Describe where identities, data and authority cross between components, then trace possible attack paths.
controls.why_it_matters: A harmless-looking input can become a privileged action after several tool or delegation steps.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Trace user content through model context, memory, MCP calls, gateways and downstream services using their actual credentials.

controls.what_it_is: Define the permitted purpose and consequences of autonomous actions and name the accountable owner.
controls.why_it_matters: An agent can act within its technical permissions while still performing an unauthorized business operation.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Document which actions require approval, which outcomes are forbidden and who handles irreversible effects or uncertainty.

controls.what_it_is: Keep dated evidence and explicitly governed exceptions for each applicable safeguard.
controls.why_it_matters: An undocumented acceptance or expired exception can conceal an untested boundary for later releases.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Record evidence, owner, expiry and compensating safeguards separately from scanner findings; justified is a decision, not proof of protection.

controls.what_it_is: Reassess the complete system when models, tools, data sources or autonomy change.
controls.why_it_matters: A previously reviewed component can gain new authority through a new integration or configuration.
controls.agent_mcp_context: A model benchmark result does not establish the safety of the harness, MCP tool inventory, credentials and deployment acting together.

controls.what_it_is: Assign each security responsibility across suppliers and the customer-operated components.
controls.why_it_matters: A safeguard can remain unimplemented when every party assumes another provider owns it.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Check which model, gateway, cloud, harness and MCP protections are inherited and which depend on your tenant configuration.

controls.what_it_is: Require verified authentication at every protected operation, including alternate routes and retries.
controls.why_it_matters: A single reachable bypass can expose tools even when the normal client login succeeds.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Distinguish protected remote HTTP operations from local stdio boundaries; test missing, malformed, revoked and expired credentials on the actual transport.

controls.what_it_is: Authorize the exact identity, tenant, operation and resource immediately before the action.
controls.why_it_matters: Being logged in does not grant permission to every tool or every other user's objects.
controls.agent_mcp_context: MCP tool names, object identifiers and agent-generated arguments must pass server-side policy for each invocation.

controls.what_it_is: Verify access-token signatures and required claims using trusted keys and explicit algorithms.
controls.why_it_matters: Decoded claims can be forged or valid for a different service if validation is incomplete.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Reject wrong audience, issuer, scope or expiry before an agent or MCP operation uses the token's claims.

controls.what_it_is: Keep caller authorization distinct from downstream service credentials.
controls.why_it_matters: A proxy may otherwise lend its broader identity to a caller or forward tokens to an unintended recipient.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Use credentials intended for the MCP resource and separately authorized downstream access instead of arbitrary inbound-token forwarding.

controls.what_it_is: Limit credential scope and lifetime and prevent unnecessary copies or disclosure.
controls.why_it_matters: A leaked long-lived token can preserve an agent's access after the original task or session ends.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Review refresh-token storage, rotation, revocation and credentials in prompts, URLs, process arguments, browser code and diagnostic output.

controls.what_it_is: Bind an OAuth authorization response to the intended transaction and registered redirect.
controls.why_it_matters: A valid-looking callback can be replayed or redirected into the wrong client or authorization flow.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Validate PKCE S256, issuer, redirect and transaction binding; an MCP client login button alone proves none of those properties.

controls.what_it_is: Constrain OAuth metadata discovery and client registration to trusted, bounded inputs.
controls.why_it_matters: Fetching attacker-chosen metadata can cross an internal network boundary before authentication completes.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Review discovery and client metadata URLs, redirects, response sizes and registration policy for the deployed MCP authorization flow.

controls.what_it_is: Carry authenticated delegation identity and bound the authority passed to another agent.
controls.why_it_matters: Text that names a trusted initiator must not create that initiator's privileges.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Limit delegation scope, depth, duration and audiences and prevent a child agent from expanding its own grant.

controls.what_it_is: Govern agent identity creation, sponsorship and retirement as a workload lifecycle.
controls.why_it_matters: Stale identities can retain credentials, registrations or cached grants after their sponsor or deployment disappears.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Test replacement, sponsor departure and compromise across the agent, MCP service and downstream permissions rather than deleting only one local account.

controls.what_it_is: Constrain network exposure and verify the origin and transport of MCP HTTP traffic.
controls.why_it_matters: An unintended browser origin, interface or unverified TLS connection can reach or impersonate a service.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Check HTTP Origin handling, local binding, remote TLS and deployed proxy behavior; a wildcard bind alone does not establish exploitability.

controls.what_it_is: Validate tool inputs and outputs against schemas and semantic limits.
controls.why_it_matters: Well-formed JSON can still request an unauthorized target, consume excessive resources or carry misleading results.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Enforce tool-specific ranges, sizes, nesting and unknown-field policy before execution; validate structured results and sanitized errors afterward.

controls.what_it_is: Treat tool descriptions, annotations, resources and results as untrusted claims.
controls.why_it_matters: A malicious server can present instructions or safety hints that influence tool selection or approval.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Inspect cross-tool instructions and keep readOnlyHint and destructiveHint separate from independent host authorization and approval.

controls.what_it_is: Bind approved tools to verified server identity and reviewed definitions, and recheck changes.
controls.why_it_matters: A tool can keep its display name while changing its arguments or effects after approval.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Check reconnects, list updates, version changes and collisions between servers; a familiar name is not a verified implementation.

controls.what_it_is: Authorize state handles and, where applicable, legacy session resumption.
controls.why_it_matters: Possession of a handle can become unauthorized access if ownership, tenant or expiry checks are missing.
controls.agent_mcp_context: The selected MCP revision determines session behavior; a legacy session identifier must never substitute for caller authentication.

controls.what_it_is: Apply host policy and user control to server-requested sampling and shared context.
controls.why_it_matters: An untrusted server may induce access to unrelated conversations or recursive model consumption.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Bound sampling context, model selection and tool access independently of the server's request and test budget amplification.

controls.what_it_is: Constrain elicitation requests and visibly identify URL interactions.
controls.why_it_matters: An apparently helpful workflow can collect credentials or direct a user to an attacker-controlled destination.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Use the selected protocol revision's form and URL rules; test cancellation, unsolicited requests, phishing links and replayed completion state.

controls.what_it_is: Enforce actual filesystem permissions independently of declared MCP roots.
controls.why_it_matters: Roots describe intended scope but cannot prevent a server process from accessing other paths.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Validate paths and symlink behavior at access time, and constrain the process identity so a claimed workspace boundary is enforceable.

controls.what_it_is: Approve local server executables and constrain their inherited environment and process access.
controls.why_it_matters: Launching a stdio server can give package code the host user's credentials and filesystem access.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Pin launch artifacts, use argument arrays and a minimal environment, separate protocol stdout from logs, and restrict process-spawn proxies.

controls.what_it_is: Apply the deployed protocol revision's capability, stream, cache and cancellation rules.
controls.why_it_matters: Assuming another revision's handshake or state model can leave authorization context inconsistent.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Test metadata and header consistency, cache separation and request continuation across the actual MCP revision rather than applying legacy session assumptions universally.

controls.what_it_is: Enforce trusted action policy at the tool execution boundary outside the model.
controls.why_it_matters: An instruction-following model can be redirected; its refusal or approval is not an access-control decision.
controls.agent_mcp_context: An injected prompt must not select privileged credentials, disable policy or expand available MCP capabilities.

controls.what_it_is: Bind human approval to the precise action that will execute.
controls.why_it_matters: A changed recipient, argument or delayed retry can exceed what the person approved.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Show concrete data disclosure and consequences, invalidate approval after changes, and test reuse and time-of-check/time-of-use races.

controls.what_it_is: Preserve the distinction between trusted instructions and externally controlled content.
controls.why_it_matters: Retrieved text, tool results or repository files can try to redirect the agent's objective or authority.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Track provenance across documents, OCR and messages; delimiters help interpretation but cannot enforce tool permissions or stop every indirect injection.

controls.what_it_is: Protect retrieval and persistent memory at both read and update boundaries.
controls.why_it_matters: Poisoned memory can influence later sessions, and incomplete retrieval filters can expose another tenant's data.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Enforce document and memory ACLs, retain provenance and verify deletion, stale context and cross-tenant vector retrieval.

controls.what_it_is: Keep delegated goals and privileges bounded across multi-agent handoffs.
controls.why_it_matters: A chain of agents can amplify authority, lose the original objective or accept impersonated messages.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Authenticate senders, validate handoff schemas and allowed transitions, and test cascading failures and conflicting instructions.

controls.what_it_is: Protect the configuration and workflow files that define agent behavior.
controls.why_it_matters: A changed skill, hook or seed file can silently add commands, access or persistence.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Inventory and review prompts, skills, memory seeds and MCP configuration; external repository instructions cannot become trusted host policy automatically.

controls.what_it_is: Apply data and destination policy to otherwise legitimate tool calls.
controls.why_it_matters: An allowed message, search or upload tool can still move sensitive context to an unauthorized recipient.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Test combined and encoded leakage paths using canary data, including URLs, tickets, telemetry and sequences of permitted actions.

controls.what_it_is: Keep untrusted values out of shell syntax and constrain allowed command arguments.
controls.why_it_matters: Agent-generated text may become a command or option rather than inert data.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Use fixed executables and validated argument arrays; test shell syntax, substitutions, hostile filenames and option injection at the same tool entry point.

controls.what_it_is: Constrain any feature that evaluates generated code in a disposable execution environment.
controls.why_it_matters: A model or tool result reaching an interpreter gains the process's effective authority.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Review eval, exec, templates and notebook tools, then enforce filesystem, network, CPU and time limits independently of the generated program.

controls.what_it_is: Parameterize query values and constrain permitted query shapes and database identities.
controls.why_it_matters: Generated queries can escape an intended object or operation even when the database connection is authorized.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Review SQL and other query languages, separate read/write identities and test the agent's reachable query path.

controls.what_it_is: Constrain file, archive and temporary-file operations at the moment of access.
controls.why_it_matters: Traversal, overwrite and link races can move data or execution beyond the approved workspace.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Review uploads, downloads, extraction and temporary files; test absolute paths, symlinks, alternate encodings and secret-directory access.

controls.what_it_is: Restrict actual network destinations, including DNS resolution and redirects.
controls.why_it_matters: A user-selected URL can turn an agent tool into a route to internal services or cloud metadata.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Validate schemes and addresses at connection time and test loopback, private and link-local IPv4/IPv6 and redirects into those ranges.

controls.what_it_is: Use data-only parsers with explicit type and resource bounds.
controls.why_it_matters: Object construction or parser expansion can execute code or exhaust a tool process.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Inspect pickle, YAML and XML paths used by agents or MCP tools; trusted artifact provenance and byte/nesting limits require separate evidence.

controls.what_it_is: Render model and tool output using context-appropriate escaping and safe URL handling.
controls.why_it_matters: Untrusted output can become executable content in a browser, terminal or exported document.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Review HTML/Markdown rendering, DOM sinks, SVG, terminal escapes and spreadsheet formulas for each output format.

controls.what_it_is: Locate embedded credential-like material and investigate its real exposure.
controls.why_it_matters: Source, fixtures or built artifacts may distribute a usable credential beyond its intended audience.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Confirm whether a detected value is real with the owner; rotate exposed credentials and address reachable history as well as the current file.

controls.what_it_is: Minimize and authorize data sent to each model or gateway recipient.
controls.why_it_matters: Prompts and tool outputs may disclose information under a provider's processing or retention terms.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Map code, memory and tool-result disclosure, document allowed data classes and destination policy, and redact before transmission where required.

controls.what_it_is: Prevent logs, traces and error messages from becoming secondary data leaks.
controls.why_it_matters: Diagnostic paths can retain credentials and private prompts even when normal responses are sanitized.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Test provider failures and exceptions as well as success paths; restrict trace storage, dashboards and exports.

controls.what_it_is: Track the origin, transformations and integrity of the data that drives AI behavior.
controls.why_it_matters: Poisoned or stale retrieval and training inputs can outlive the event that introduced them.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Maintain owner/version evidence for datasets, corpora and memory seeds and demonstrate quarantine, removal and replacement of unexpected content.

controls.what_it_is: Apply retention and deletion across derived and replicated data.
controls.why_it_matters: Deleting a source record may leave retrievable embeddings, cached prompts or provider-held copies.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Test expiry and removal across memory, caches, artifacts, backups and dependent access grants rather than checking one database row.

controls.what_it_is: Protect stored data with restricted identities, key separation and tested access controls.
controls.why_it_matters: Encryption settings alone cannot stop an authorized but overprivileged agent identity from reading data.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Verify tenant and operational-role boundaries, key rotation and backup access together with storage and transport configuration.

controls.what_it_is: Record and constrain the executable versions and immutable artifacts used by the system.
controls.why_it_matters: A floating dependency or runtime install can change the code behind an approved agent or MCP server.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Review effective lockfiles, images, models and plugins and flag package sources or remote scripts outside approved release paths.

controls.what_it_is: Assess known vulnerabilities and maintenance status in the resolved dependencies.
controls.why_it_matters: An apparently clean source scan can still ship a vulnerable or unsupported library or base image.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Use appropriate advisory tooling, record database age and resolved versions, and assess reachability and fix availability; this scanner does not query CVE feeds.

controls.what_it_is: Verify artifact identity, publisher trust and build provenance before enabling it.
controls.why_it_matters: A valid digest can identify malicious bytes just as precisely as trusted bytes.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Check signatures, publisher identity and origin for server packages and model artifacts, including model-loader serialization behavior.

controls.what_it_is: Protect the build and release path and the credentials it can access.
controls.why_it_matters: Untrusted changes to workflows or agent configuration may execute with deployment authority.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Review CI permissions, action references, build scripts and promotion controls, especially contributions that can alter approved tool policies.

controls.what_it_is: Use restrictive runtime identities and deployment boundaries around agent execution.
controls.why_it_matters: Root, privileged mounts or runtime sockets can turn a tool compromise into broader host access.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Separate execution from control-plane credentials and audit storage; test capabilities, network policy and management exposure in the actual deployment.

controls.what_it_is: Separate training, evaluation and production authority when developing models.
controls.why_it_matters: An untrusted training job or altered adapter could replace an approved production artifact.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Protect datasets, weights, registries and release permissions independently and demonstrate that development identities cannot promote arbitrary model state.

controls.what_it_is: Produce an attributable and protected history of security-relevant actions.
controls.why_it_matters: Without correlated identities and outcomes, an agent incident may be impossible to reconstruct.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Record the initiator, delegated identity, tool/version, necessary redacted argument context, policy decision and outcome, and prevent the agent from erasing that evidence.

controls.what_it_is: Enforce resource and spending budgets across the complete unit of work.
controls.why_it_matters: Loops, retries and child agents can multiply consumption beyond a per-request limit.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Bound iterations, calls, tokens, bytes, elapsed time and concurrency with server-enforced accounting that survives delegation and retries.

controls.what_it_is: Make cancellation revoke future work and stop consequential effects.
controls.why_it_matters: Stopping a user interface does not necessarily cancel queued actions, child processes or usable credentials.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Measure stop latency and test whether disconnected or cancelled MCP/agent requests can still commit side effects.

controls.what_it_is: Keep failure and recovery paths from widening authority or repeating side effects.
controls.why_it_matters: A timeout, fallback or retry can execute an action twice or bypass a failed policy check.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Deny or escalate on identity/approval failures and test idempotency, partial commits and alternate-model or tool paths.

controls.what_it_is: Detect unusual behavior and restore trusted system state after harmful changes.
controls.why_it_matters: Unexpected destinations or scope growth can remain invisible until many automated actions have occurred.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Seed observable events to verify alerts, and test rollback of prompts, models, tools, policies and poisoned memory.

controls.what_it_is: Prepare and exercise an incident response process for agent-specific failures.
controls.why_it_matters: Stopping an agent without revoking credentials or preserving evidence may leave the compromise active.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Practice isolation, owner notification, recovery and approved disclosure channels while protecting sensitive investigation data.

controls.what_it_is: Measure adversarial safety alongside authorized task completion in representative workflows.
controls.why_it_matters: A defense that blocks every useful action can appear safe, while a model-only score misses tool side effects.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Run paired benign and hostile external-content cases and record attacker success, useful-task success, false blocks and unauthorized effects.

controls.what_it_is: Repeat and vary adversarial scenarios under a stated attacker budget.
controls.why_it_matters: A single fixed prompt or aggregate average can hide failures that appear with another placement or attempt.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Record model and harness versions, modalities, sample counts and per-scenario uncertainty when retesting changed defenses.

controls.what_it_is: Exercise authentication and protocol abuse against the actual MCP revision in an isolated environment.
controls.why_it_matters: Correct-looking source does not establish how a deployed transport handles hostile peers or malformed state.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Test wrong-audience tokens, origins, malicious servers and protocol inputs with sanitized request/response evidence.

controls.what_it_is: Test isolation using distinct principals across every stateful surface.
controls.why_it_matters: An authorization check may work on objects but fail on caches, memory, subscriptions or resumed work.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Attempt cross-user and cross-agent access after delegation, reconnect, concurrency and revocation, retaining denied-access evidence.

controls.what_it_is: Test forbidden-action boundaries across approvals, policy and sandbox alternatives.
controls.why_it_matters: A safeguard on one execution path may be bypassed through a different tool, retry or child agent.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Use explicit canaries and verify consistent enforcement after hostile content, tool substitution and delayed execution.

controls.what_it_is: Apply conventional application security validation to the interfaces agents can reach.
controls.why_it_matters: AI-specific controls do not replace ordinary access control, injection prevention or dependency review.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Combine language-aware analysis, secrets/dependency tools and authorized integration tests against reachable application behavior.

controls.what_it_is: Exercise resource exhaustion and validate the supporting telemetry and shutdown path.
controls.why_it_matters: A quota can fail operationally if slow peers, stream floods or unavailable dependencies defeat accounting or alerts.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Test oversized traffic, recursive work and repeated failures together with attribution, cancellation and leakage prevention.

controls.what_it_is: Evaluate the optional security reviewer as another untrusted, fallible component.
controls.why_it_matters: A model may accept repository instructions, invent evidence or emit malformed judgments.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Use labeled cases and hostile inputs, validate identifiers/citations/output shape, preserve deterministic findings and report omissions and model variability.

controls.what_it_is: Evaluate model-layer threats when hosting, acquiring or customizing models.
controls.why_it_matters: Behavioral triggers, extraction or training-data disclosure may not be visible in application source patterns.
controls.agent_mcp_context: Set explicit attacker access and query budgets, identify the tested model/adapters and retain measured limits before promoting a new model.
